utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. On this last day of hearings before we resume our work at the beginning of August, I would like to welcome all of those in the courtroom, the representatives of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, as well as the accused. First of all, I would like to pay tribute to our registrar who unfortunately is going to leave us for the OSCE in Belgrade for -- to assume high functions, and I congratulate him, but unfortunately it's already the third registrar who is leaving us, so I hope that our fourth registrar will stay with us a bit longer. But, Mr. Marco Bonabello, we thank you for all that you have done for us in helping the Trial Chamber with great efficiency, and on behalf of my colleagues I can only wish you all the best for your future success in your new functions that will be in Belgrade as of the end of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of the accused and the Defence, may I be associated with what Your Honour has said. We also thank Marco for his hard work and good humour. We're also sorry to have driven away yet another registrar, but we wish him very well in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could add the congratulations of the Prosecution. Marco has assured me that his departure is not in any way linked to my arrival in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Stringer. Now, very quickly, the Trial Chamber would like to hear the oral observations of the Defence, but the Defence counsel will only have two minutes, in fact, it's very technical. The Prosecution addressed to us on the 11th of July a request for being dispensed from the guideline 6(A)(iv). The topic was already addressed during the 65 ter Conference that took place recently. We have the submissions. The Defence has received them as well. The Trial Chamber is going to hand down a written ruling very shortly, but I will give Mr. Karnavas a couple of minutes to -- for the observations of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Concerning this matter, Your Honour. Very well. I thought I had made my point very clear the other day. I think that the decision made by the Trial Chamber initially was a good one. I think that the Prosecution should just simply abide by it. It's -- the problem that we have here is that the Prosecution, by way of a tsunami, is overwhelming us with documents, and the only way to counter this tsunami approach is to force them to go through those documents and articulate with precision why is it that they need these documents and how they're related and how they're linked. If you may recall, Mr. President, this was something that you had initiated and had requested prior to the commencement of the trial and I dare say had we taken that approach at the very beginning and maybe streamlined the indictment we wouldn't be in the position that we are here today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. I think that the other Defence counsels would like to join in?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, good afternoon. In connection with this request by the Prosecution, I wish to say the following: Granting the motion would invalidate the rule that evidence is introduced through witnesses. If we are invalidating this rule or at least raising this to the level of a rule, I think we should reconsider changing Rule 6 so that the Defence will also be able to tender documents not through witnesses under the same rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber will hand down a written request on that question quite quickly. I have three oral decisions to read. I will go quickly because we don't have much time today. Oral decision on the request of the Prosecution for admission of documents relating to the testimony of Josip Praljak. On the 4th of July, 2007, the Prosecution filed a written motion for the admittance of 26 documents related to the testimony of Josip Praljak pursuant to Rule 89(C) as well as guideline number 6 set forth in the Trial Chamber's ruling of 29 November 2006. The Trial Chamber first of all wants to recall that in a decision of April 3rd, 2007, it has already ruled on the request for admission of documents submitted through Witness Josip Praljak. Moreover, guideline number 6 authorises the Prosecution to submit written requests after the end of the presentation of evidence related to a municipality or a specific topic and not related to a particular witness. That being said, the Trial Chamber notes that the documents requested for admission pertain to the administration and management of the Heliodrom. The Chamber also observes that in paragraph 7 of its motion the Prosecution announces that it intends to file shortly a written motion for the admission of documents pertaining to the Heliodrom. For these reasons and for the sake of judicial efficiency, the Trial Chamber decides to review the current request of the Prosecution for admission of documents at the same time as the motion that it will file shortly for admission of documents pertaining to the Heliodrom. Thus the Trial Chamber decides to defer its ruling on the written motion of the Prosecution dated July 4, 2007. Very well. So in a nutshell, the Trial Chamber will hand down a ruling that will encompass both the motion of July 4th, 2007, and the motion regarding all of the documents pertaining to the Heliodrom. That is the meaning of the first oral decision. Second oral decision. Regarding the Defence's motion to prolong its deadline for answering motions of the Prosecution during the conference of the legal officer on 9th of July, 2007, 65 ter. The Defence asked for an extension of its deadline to the 1st of October to answer the requests of the Prosecution. First of all, the request for the admission of evidence pursuant to Article 92 bis relating to the municipality of Mostar filed by the Prosecution on the 4th of July, 2007. Second request, the request for admission of evidence, documentary evidence, relating to the municipality of Mostar filed by the Prosecution on the 4th of July, 2007. And third request, the request for admission of evidence, documentary evidence, relating to the municipality of Vares filed by the Prosecution on the 5th of July, 2007. And the fourth request, the request for the admission of 26 exhibits following the appearance of the Witness Praljak filed by the Prosecution on the 4th of July, 2007. The Prosecution has not opposed this request for an extension of the deadline. The Trial Chamber notes that pursuant to Rule 126 bis, answers to the motions or requests must be submitted on the 18th and 19th of July, 2007. Nonetheless, given the great number of pending requests to which the Defence must provide an answer, the Trial Chamber feels that it would be appropriate to grant an extension of the deadline till the 24th of September, 2007, for the motions one, two, and three. As to the answers to the request for admission of 26 exhibits, the fourth motion or request, the Trial Chamber recalls that it has just decided to defer its ruling on that request waiting for the Prosecution's next motion that it will file shortly regarding documents pertaining to the Heliodrom. Hence the Defence will be able to file one single response to those two motions taken together. Thus in a nutshell, for the first three motions the Defence has until the 24th of September and not the 1st of October. As to the fourth motion, it will be joined with the motion to come regarding the Heliodrom and the Defence can reply to both requests together. And now the final oral decision, and I have to hurry. Oral decision amending the deadlines granted for response to the Prosecution's request to add exhibits to the 65 ter list. On the 26th of June, 2007, the Prosecution filed a motion requesting leave from the Trial Chamber to add 28 exhibits to the 65 ter list. By oral decision of the 4th of July, 2007, the Trial Chamber had granted an extension of the deadline to the Defence teams to file replies to that motion, deadline set at the 10th of September, 2007. Nonetheless, given time constraints links to the fact that the witness whose name I will not mention is to appear shortly I will not mention his name but everyone must know who it is, the Trial Chamber wants to reverse the decision or the ruling handed down on the 4th of July, 2007, and grants the Defence a deadline until the 20th of August, 2007. Well, we were obliged to shorten this deadline because there is real urgency since this witness may appear shortly. So you have until the 20th of August for the matters relating to the 28 documents added to the 65 ter list. And now we shall bring in the witness without further ado. I would beg all of you not waste any time and scrupulously abide by the timing that I indicated to you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Good afternoon, Colonel. So the cross-examination shall be pursued. I wish you a warm welcome. As you know, your appearance will come to an end. Can you hear me now? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As I was saying, as you know the hearing today will come to a end at 4.25. Of course, it's even better if we can finish earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: May I just check that you have both the Prosecution bundle and the pink Stojic document bundle in front of you, please?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: If my calculation is right, you spent a total of about 10 weeks in Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right? Let me help you by saying that you arrived in late May, you left in late August, and I think you were on leave for about two weeks in July; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: By my -- I think that I was one week away, not two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: 10 or 11 weeks then. During that time you told us you did not learn to speak B/C/S apart from what I think a courtesy command of the language; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some expressions, yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Rather like my Dutch probably. You could say good morning and ask for a cup of coffee and so on.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the way, without any accent. You did it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: As an ECMM monitor, sir, was it important to you to remain neutral as between the warring parties?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paramount importance, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Paramount importance. It was also important to you to obtain information from whatever sources you could. Would that be true?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And I think you've testified on a previous occasion in the Tuta and Stela case that you were in pretty much daily contact with SpaBat and other organisations in the theatre?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: In fact, during your testimony in this trial, you -- you said that you'd put together what you described as a network of a kind, which I found an interesting phrase. That's a phrase that one uses in connection with intelligence operations, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not my intention to use it in the sense of intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I want to go back to a subject that my colleague Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic dealt with yesterday. I'm sorry to be repetitive but it is important to what I have to ask you. You told us, I think, that there was a pool of interpreters available for the use of the monitors in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And since you didn't speak the language, it was obviously important for you to have access to an interpreter for all the meetings that you attended.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And M2, your unit, did not use interpreters from the pool but made use of the services of this Muslim woman that we have discussed.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was a part of the pool, but located in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I see. And in fact, during the meetings that you had, you used this -- by you now I mean M2, you used this particular interpreter on an exclusive basis, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially when we went downtown Mostar, yeah, because in Siroki Brijeg we -- we used, of course, the other ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. So all the meetings that you had in Mostar you would use this particular interpreter.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I think that we, in my time frame, used her always, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. Your relationship with her was such that you would pick her up from her house and then take her back after her work was finished; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And it extended on at least one occasion that we know about to visiting her home for the purpose of having coffee with members of her family.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least once.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: You also told us, I don't want to go back over this ground too much, but using a Muslim interpreter was a deliberate choice.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And a point that did not come out yesterday but you mentioned in your statement to the Prosecutor's office, you mentioned that this interpreter's father had at some point been imprisoned by the HVO. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't mention that probably in my -- you mean two days ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: No, sir. I mean in the written statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, the first time you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: When you were interviewed by representatives of the Prosecutor's office in August 2001. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: You made a written witness statement?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep. Well, it is in that statement, it's clear that I --

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Let me just read you what you said. This is on page 2 of the English version. You said -- I'm not going to read it all, but you said: "She was studying English at the university. Her father had been imprisoned by the HVO," and then you went on with other information.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then it's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: All right. Now, in addition to being an interpreter, this lady also was a source of information, wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Well, you've testified, have you not, that she gave you information many times. I think that was language you used in the Tuta and Stela case.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I explained that yesterday, I think, that in principle she was only in -- translating when she was asked to do so. But at the same time, she came sometimes with stories you heard in the evening or at night, the next day in the morning, and gave us that kind of information. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And that was important to you, because your unit did not move around and work after dark?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And among the pieces of information, for example, that she gave you on one occasion was the number of expelled Muslims. Five thousand; right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall if it came from her, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Well, I was referring to your -- your testimony in the -- in the Tuta and Stela case at page 7396 of the transcript, and you had said that the -- that it was hard to get an exact number of people who were arrested or expelled, and you said that it came from a reliable source, and then you added: "That was our interpreter at that time." I don't want to take the time, but does that refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was at the -- at the 30th of June, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I think the 5th of July, but no matter. We'll move on. She also gave you information, did she not, that suggested that -- that Tuta might have an office in the Ministry of Defence building? That was another piece of information she gave you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only from her. We heard that, for instance, from our predecessors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. But you did get that from her as well, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she went there with us, so she was -- she was well aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: In the Tuta and Stela case you described her as being well-informed about events locally; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the west bank for that part of the -- her own environment, I suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Now, the kind of information that she gave you was relating to what we might call crimes or bad acts committed by the HVO against the Muslim population; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you refer to -- to let's say the notes and the reports, yes, we mentioned here, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Did she ever during the time she worked with you provide any information about any crimes committed against Bosnian Croats by Muslim population or the army and Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went there many times, and she was, on our request, interviewing people about that kind of allegations as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Well, I asked you a very precise question, Colonel. Did she ever provide you information about crimes committed by Muslims or the armija against Bosnian Croats?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: As a member of the interpreters pool, was she paid a salary by the -- by the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved in -- in that kind of things, and I really don't recall, but I guess that she got some -- some money for the work, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Well, the point of my question is this really: Was she paid additional money for pieces of information that she supplied to you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Definitely not.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: The information that she provided to you made its way into your reports, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it was important and verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Would it not be true to say, Colonel, that this lady, rather than an interpreter, was in fact your agent, using the status of interpreter as a cover? Do you understand what I mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess what -- what you mean, but definitely not to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Definitely not.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: All right. And you said yesterday that you don't remember how she was recruited. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that in detail, no, no. Unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: May we move into private session just for a moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Did ever occur to you, Colonel, that using this lady as an interpreter might be a problem in terms of your neutrality as between the warring parties?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in the fact that sometimes we were threatened having her in our car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: All right. Now, you testified that SpaBat provided you with what we might call a list of members of the HVO who were regarded as Hawks and those who were regarded as Doves. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And perhaps we could settle on a definition of exactly what a Hawk means, because I think in the course of your testimony two days ago you -- you told us that Hawk meant a strong nationalist; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A hard-liner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: A hard-liner.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Whereas in the statement that you gave to the Prosecutor, you said that a Hawk meant somebody who wanted to fight and was not inclined to negotiate. Which of those definitions would you like to go with today?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I said that before?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I -- I refer to the last statement I made about that definition.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: By the way, did SpaBat give you a list of Hawks on the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And you said that the list that SpaBat gave you corresponded with your own assessment.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only for a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. Including Mr. Stojic?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And that was based upon your meetings with Mr. Stojic, was it?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Now, is this right, sir, that every word that you exchanged with Mr. Stojic during those meetings was exchanged through the medium of your interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That hard to say every word, because I think Mr. Stojic was able to understand English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: You're saying that Mr. Stojic understands English?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I supposed that he understands English as well. But you are right by the remark that we used our interpreter in that kind of situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I want to be very clear about this. Did Mr. Stojic, on any occasion, speak English to you during a meeting that you had with him?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: So he was speaking Croatian.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Right. Well, let me go back to the question I previously asked you then. Is it right to say that the words that were exchanged between Mr. Stojic and yourself were exchanged through the medium of the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And so it was based upon what the interpreter told you that Mr. Stojic said that you formed the impression that he was a Hawk?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not only of course, as I said yesterday, exactly the text what was -- what was translated, but it was also the performance and -- and the way of acting, of course. For me, because you ask my opinion about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Sir, as a senior officer in the Dutch army, have you had occasion during your career to write reports on junior officers?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And these reports would deal with their performance and character as officers; right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Normally. Because perhaps the promotion of an officer might depend on what you said in a report, yes?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. You'd want to have a lot more information than you had about Mr. Stojic before informing a judgement on an officer's character, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I'll move on. Do you recall, sir, that you had a meeting with Mr. Stojic, I think you've testified about it, on the 16th of June, 1993, in which you discussed with him, among other things, the shooting of the Spanish officer, Lieutenant Aguilar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And you subsequently wrote in your report, I don't need to refer you to it but if you want to look it's P 02806, that Mr. Stojic had said that the snipers in the blue bank building were under control. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Now, because of the rules of the Tribunal, I'm -- I'm going to -- even though I think this may be a little pointless, but I'm going to put it to you that Mr. Stojic did not in fact say any such thing, but of course you had no means of knowing that except what your interpreter told you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Because whatever he said, he said in Croatian. Yes?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Is that a yes?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Okay. Would you please look in the Stojic binder and find an exhibit for me. This will be 2D 00116, please. It should be the third document in the binder, I think. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Could you please tell me if you've ever seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: While that's happening, Your Honour, may I just ask how I'm doing for time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Could I ask the registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Normally, you were supposed to go to 2.50, but oral decisions took me some time, about five to 10 minutes. So you'll have -- you have 10 more minutes. You have to five to 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: You say you've not seen that document before; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: All right. Let me nonetheless ask you whether you are aware of any of the matters that are described, this is a letter dated the 14th of June, 1993, from Mr. Stojic, addressed to the Spanish minister of defence in Madrid, and it records the fact that that a joint investigation was carried out into the shooting of the lieutenant by the -- by SpaBat and also by officers of the Ministry of Defence. Were you familiar with the fact that such an investigation had occurred?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we knew that there were more than one investigations ongoing. So this probably is one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: If you would -- if you would look at the second page of this document in the English version. I can't -- because of lack of time I can't go through all the findings, but the Trial Chamber will be able to read them, but there's a paragraph beginning on the second page, "Based on everything we conclude." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And it says that: "We conclude that the UNPROFOR vehicle was shot from the Muslim military positions at the Bristol Hotel." First of all, were you aware that the ABiH did in fact have a position situated in the Bristol Hotel?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were aware that it was on -- on the west line, huh? What you were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were aware of that, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Were you aware that a finding had been made in this inquiry that shot could have come from that position in the Bristol Hotel? Have you heard that before today?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: All right. Would you also look at I think what should be the next document 2D 00117. Yes. Next document in there, please.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And this is a very similar document, and the only question that I want to ask you about this is whether you may have seen this document before. It's signed by Mr. Lukic, one of Mr. Stojic's assistants. It deals with broadly the same facts.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: All right. Referring to your own testimony in this trial about the -- the shooting of the Spanish lieutenant, I think it's possible that the -- the Trial Chamber may -- may have been given the impression, I'm referring now to page 47 of the transcript of the 10th of July, line 25, may have been given the impression that you were actually present for this event, but that's not the case, is it?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: You heard about it later.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And you -- you gave the Trial Chamber your opinion about where the shot may have come from, but just to make this absolutely clear, this was based upon information that was provided to you.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And I think you made some kind of comparison, at least in your own mind, between that event and an event that had occurred when your vehicle was in fact fired upon in the same general area?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but was not the same spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Not the same spot, no. If you would look, please, at -- this will be in the Prosecution binder, Exhibit number P 02635. In the Prosecution binder. 02635. Tell me when you've got it, please.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: This is a daily report from team M2, dated the 4th of June, 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And if you look at item 8, this is the second page in the English version, it records that your car was fired at at 1435 hours, and -- you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And then a few further lines down you say: "We do not know who shot us (HVO or armija) because in this area both parts are mixed. We guess, we guess from the direction of the impact that the sniper was in one building belonging to the HVO." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: That was the language you use.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the story.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: So we can conclude from that you were not able to ascertain with any degree of certainty where the shot came from?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, specific case, but it was not the same spot, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: If I may just have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel. Your Honour, that concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Murphy. Mr. Praljak, you have 35 minutes, and at 3.30, I will turn the mike off because I will need to give the floor to Ms. Alaburic. But you have the floor now for 35 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Colonel. I don't have much time, so I'll ask you to be militarily precise and let's look at Prosecution document first, 02634 is the number. P 0264. And it is the photograph of your car. You can see a large hole above the window here. Is that hole on the window a hole caused by a bullet as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could we just get that exhibit number again? I don't think we got it in the English channel.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P 02634. P 02634. It is the photograph of the car.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Have you got it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: We see something on the window here. Is that a hit?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: What about the thing we see up above the right-hand corner of the window. Is that a hit?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, where was the car hit then?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, then I misunderstood you. On the two windows that are not hits. The hit is just in between, on the right shelf of the car. In front, just in front of the photograph. Between the two windows. That is the hit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, you mean, the small black dot between the two windows. Is that it? On the back of the car. Could you indicate it for us, please, using your pencil? On the monitor, use your pencil and point to the place where the car was hit.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So that's where it was hit. Thank you. When you got out of the vehicle did you happen to look at the angle that the hit came from? Because obviously the hole isn't a regular shape. In fact, it's difficult to discern that it is a hole at all. But let's move on. Look at 2635. That's the next page in the document. And you talk about this event, and you say that you were on the Old Bridge, on Tito -- on the Tito Bridge. Is that right? Were you on the Tito Bridge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, do you need an IC number for this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... will become Exhibit IC 629.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So you were on the Tito Bridge when this happened; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And you were moving from the west towards the east; right? From the area under HVO control towards the area under BH army control; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now please take a look at my documents document 3D 00746. 3D 00746 is the document number. Do you agree with me when I say that this photograph was taken from the Tito Bridge and looking west? You see Hotel Bristol and the street ahead; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: From this point, if you were there either to the left or to the right, can you see the secondary school or the glass bank? Can you see that from this spot here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I intervene. It must be clarified that the picture is actually not taken from a spot on the bridge but from quite -- it's difficult to estimate because one does not know the focus, but one quite a distance from the bridge. One sees the full bridge from beginning to end on the picture.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour Judge Trechsel. This is on -- in the middle of the bridge, exactly in the middle of the bridge, to the left, which would give a better view of the glass bank because it is located on the right. But I'm going to show a whole set of photographs to show you that that is indeed the case, and I think the Judges will be able to take a Ph.D. on the subject of bridges and vantage points.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So this is facing west; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I correct myself. I was looking at the next picture.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I have been looking at the next picture, and that was my error, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the witness gave an affirmative answer and said that that was indeed from the position of the Tito Bridge looking westward.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, Witness, look at the next photograph, please, which moves towards the east and shows the bridge in full view. 3D 00746. And the photograph number is 526, 0526. So is this the right photograph? You can see the Tito Bridge and facing HVO positions. Right, Witness? Just turn the page, sir. The next page. You can look at my set of photographs. 526 is the number. That's it there. You have it on the screen. Is that right? The Bristol Hotel? The Tito Bridge? Do you recognise this, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it's definitely not taken on the 4th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: No. No. It was taken a while ago, but nothing has changed, and Their Honours had these photographs. Now take a look at the next photograph in this series. Let's move on if we may. Taken further back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph is important. Colonel, on this photograph that is in front of our screen, with the pen could you fell us what direction the car was going, your car was going?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: No, Witness, you were moving in the opposite direction. From the west to the east. So your direction isn't towards the HVO positions as you've just indicated but the opposite, at least according to your statement, because had you been moving in that direction then the bullet certainly would have come from the BH army side, whereas here we're still debating the point, and we're going to clarify it. So think about it some more. You were moving towards us like the car with the lights switched on, headlights switched on, regardless of where you were on the bridge. That was the direction you were moving in, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, this is why I asked that you give us the direction the car was going. This is absolutely essential.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just make a suggestion that perhaps assists the witness so it can move faster. Perhaps he could be asked whether he recognises the large hill feature in the background, what that is, and whether that helps him orientate which side of the river he's looking across to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What exactly is this hill in the back? Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. That is Hum. The hill called Hum.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: No, Witness, that is not Hum hill. It's the road you took towards Siroki Brijeg. Hum hill is to the left, and we've already seen that on the maps quite a way to the left, and you can't see it on this photograph. To be quite frank, I'm a little surprised, because you're a professional soldier. Now, the road you can see up in the hill is the road leading to Siroki Brijeg, which you passed dozens of times. And you also passed along this road here dozens of times across the Defence lines on both sides. But if you did move towards us, towards the people there, then that direction would be from the HVO positions moving towards the BH army positions. That's what you said. That's how you described it. Otherwise, the entire problem of where you were hit and how you were hit is senseless.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, let me shortly comment on that. I think it has nothing to do with my profession. It has to do with the fact that it's 14 years ago. So you confront me with this photograph, and it takes some time to make some orientation, because it's 14 years ago, and I think it's fair to take that in consideration.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. I have nothing against that. Do you recognise the Bristol Hotel on the right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you recognise the road up there moving towards Spanish Square? The square was named Spanish Square because of the death of the Spanish officer. So you were moving from Spanish Square, and you were hit while on the bridge, from top to bottom, going from top to bottom. Can you confirm that? If you can, then draw an arrow for the direction you were moving in and your position on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have difficulties with this picture. Let's make that clear, sir. And the statement I made is also clear. That means that my interpretation here of the picture is wrong, then it is the other way around than what I just noted here on the screen with the pen. I don't have any problem to explain you that in this way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Colonel, would you draw in after everything that you have said and giving thought to you -- to it, what was your direction, the direction in which you moved? Colonel, why don't you take a look at the next photograph. It might be easier for you. Let's take a look at the following photograph, 551. The next one in the file. The number is 551. And on the right-hand side you can see something that used to be the Neretva Hotel, which has not been reconstructed. It's still in ruins. Does that make the situation of this Musala square, the Tito Bridge, on the right the Neretva Hotel, on the right the Bristol Hotel, does this make it any clearer? Can you find your bearings better?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you draw in the direction you moved in now?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was -- okay. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Okay. May I have an IC number for the photograph? No, it has a number. Right. It has a number. We don't need an IC number. Yes, it does I'm told. An IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this picture will become IC 630.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Another question: Witness, did you ever stand in this spot and, if so, can you see either the secondary school building or the glass bank from here? Because you said that it was possible that your vehicle might have been shot at from those two positions. So can you see the glass bank or the gymnasium, the secondary school building?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note -- I don't know the spot where this photograph was taken, but I don't see it on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now let's take a look at Exhibit 3D 00844. 3D 00844. That's right. 3D 00844. And it is the second photograph with the number 229. Take a look at that photograph, and do you agree with me when I say that the photograph was taken from Spanish Square? You can see the Spanish Square itself. And then the street leading downwards leads towards Tito's Bridge, the Tito Bridge. Is that correct to the best of your recollections?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I have the right picture here on my screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes, you do. This is Spanish Square. Do you agree that to the best of your knowledge the buildings on the right and on the left, is that where the BH army had its positions? Is this the Bulevar in front? And the buildings on the left and right, were they all under BH army control, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's hard to say when I look to this picture what was taken maybe recently. I even never heard of the Spanish Square, so -- it was -- it was probably easier for me to recognise and give answers on your questions when you provide me with photographs from -- from that specific time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The building on the left, this dilapidated building, damaged building, it hasn't changed since then. Buildings can be renovated, but this square, regardless of its name, looked empty in your time as well, and this building was in the same condition. Do you remember passing by and going down towards Tito's bridge?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, it's quite difficult for me now to give that kind of answers when I see this picture, because the environment is definitely changed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. Would you please look at this chessboard. Let's remember it, and then we'll move on to photograph 232. 3D 00844, and the photograph is 232. Is this the glass bank you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It looks the same still.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: If we saw that chessboard a little while ago, if you stand in the spot from which you can look towards Tito's bridge, is the glass bank far right? It's to the left of the chessboard. So is it to the left at least a hundred or a hundred and fifty metres away to the left? You can look at the previous photograph and you will see the chessboard. Then you can look at the position of the glass bank. Is it about a hundred to a hundred and fifty metres to the left? Is this correct to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I try to orientate it, and I think it's to the right. I mean the first picture.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. Could I have an IC number for both these documents, 229 and 232?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the witness did not write or note anything on 844. Colonel, on the picture 844 where you see the glass building, could you note an X so that we know that that's the glass building that you recognised on that picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the picture on the screen, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The building on the right, that's what we called the blue bank building. I can point it out by the pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you note blue bank.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, let's give it an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this photo will become Exhibit IC 631.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, now please look at 3D 01059. 3D 01059. That's the next photograph. And my question is you never climbed up onto the first or second floor of that bank? You never saw the view from that bank; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Myself, no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, look then at photograph 3D 01059. This photograph was taken from the glass bank. Can you indicate, because you know where the mosque was, where the ruined buildings, were, can you indicate where Tito's bridge would be here. You see the street leading from the square towards the east. Where would Tito's bridge be in this photograph? And tell me, first of all, assuming that this bank was actually taken from the glass bank, and we have just seen the position of the bank, can one see Tito's bridge on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on this photograph, because --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you put an arrow to indicate where it should be?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere here, I think, but once again with the new buildings it's hard to see for me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, regardless of the renovated buildings, can you tell us were the buildings there, they were damaged but not completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I'm going to object at this point. I think it's unfair to ask the witness to guess at the position of the Tito Bridge on the basis of a photograph that clearly has reconstruction evident in it, and it's really not helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. What I observe is that if the picture is taken from the blue bank building, we don't see the Tito Bridge, and it's impossible for a sniper to hit a vehicle that would be driving along Tito bridge from this standpoint except if the white building that we see behind the two buildings that are in ruins did not exist at the time. If, at the time, that building did not exist, perhaps, but as we see it now it is impossible to see Tito Bridge. Please proceed, Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: While -- if you allow just in addition to what the President just said, we have seen on the previous picture that this blue bank building is a very big building. It's very large, very high. It's not very deep but it's large and high. And we do not, of course, know from which spot of the building the picture is taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, I hope that your photographer took the picture from the highest point possible within the building.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This photograph was taken from the highest point of this building. And even had the building had 20 more floors, I assert that even then one would not have been able to see Tito's bridge from it. But unfortunately because I'm short of time I cannot go into further detail in this respect. Could the witness now please be shown -- can this photograph be given an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become IC 632, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to give the witness a blank piece of paper for him to sketch a map, but since we don't have time could the usher take a map to the witness. And if Your Honours ever visit Mostar again in the course of these proceedings, you will be able to stand on Tito's bridge and see for yourselves what can be seen from it. Could this be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we have an exhibit number for this exhibit, this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had a blank map, and I wanted the witness to inscribe everything in it, but as time is short I won't do that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, number 1. Can you see number 1 up here? Is this something that used to be called the surgical hospital, Kirurgija?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an exhibit that has already been admitted through another witness. 3D 01060, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do I have this in the materials that have been provided by the accused? Is this in the papers that have come to us?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's in the binder. 3D 01060. 3D 01060.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm waiting for the mike. Yes. To get this clear, the map underneath is the same but the one we have now on the ELMO has marks which 3D 01060 has not. So it is not really the same document. It is the a different document on the same basis.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Something wrong with my mike. General Praljak said that he had a blank map which he wanted to show to the witness, but in order to save time he has put in the positions himself. We were unable to photocopy this for everyone because we hadn't prepared it beforehand, so that now this map with the marks put in by the general is being put on the ELMO. The map itself is identical. It's the same map of Mostar, which has already been admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I fully understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, on the basis of that I object to this procedure. Certainly counsel wouldn't be allowed to make their own markings and offer evidence in this way, and I think it's fairer for the witness if he's to be given a map, give him a blank map and ask him if he's able to note locations, rather than confirming those suggested to him 14 years later.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have already worked in this same way with maps of Mostar and we are saving time this way. This is a map of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, would you say what is represented by numbers 1 through 9 so we can go very quickly?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's very simple, because 14 years have elapsed and my time is running out. I've been given 10 minutes by Ms. Alaburic. If I use the witness to make these markings, I will need an hour. If Your Honours give me an hour, I can ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: But, Witness, please, look at number 1, number 1 on the map. Is this what we used to call Kirurgija, the surgical ward, which was mentioned here as place where everybody was supposed to receive treatment? Is it true that this is the surgical ward, Kirurgija?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I first clarify, sir, that we used a car in the combat zone and not a helicopter. So that is the first problem now. I am used to use a map what is oriented with a sign in the military profession to the north. I can't find it here. So let's first orientate the map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Might I make a suggestion, Mr. President? We could take a break at this point, give the gentleman an opportunity to look at the blank map that Mr. Praljak had, and then -- which would have the orientation, and this would give -- so we could save some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the best is to take a short break --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to give the witness another which is even clearer than this one so that he can take a look at this one, too, because the witness has established that that hospital could not be used for the purpose proposed by Mr. Bagaric because of the vicinity of the line. So I have to ask whether this hospital operated all the time, whether the operations were carried out there all the time, how far away the line was. This is very important. So I'm asking for a little additional time, not a lot, because I've lost a lot of time trying to jog the witness's memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll take the traditional break but just 15 minutes, and that will give the witness time to study the maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing may resume. Mr. Praljak, please be extremely quick.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, under number 1, you have the Kirurgija, or surgery ward, or as you refer to it as the old hospital. Were you ever in the hospital yourself?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in, but we were visit it by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I'm sorry but this implies that the witness has identified number 1 as that specific location, the war hospital, and I want -- I think the record needs to be clear about what the witness has identified versus what the accused is suggesting to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Colonel, if number 1 is the war hospital, would you please specify that you have identified as such?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By my knowledge the war hospital, and it is better shown on the aerial picture I have here in front, is on the drawn map in front of this number 2 and not number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: I seem to have lost -- well, I haven't got the map on the screen. Could you put the large map back on the ELMO, please. That's right. Let's see it on the ELMO. Now, number 1. Do you identify number 1 as being something called the new hospital in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Right. Now, did you ever go inside that hospital?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The new hospital, yeah, several times.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Right. Did you ever ask how the hospital was financed?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Right. Did you ever ask what the ethnic composition of the doctors in the hospital was?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war or during the conflict, mixed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: During the conflict, while you were there.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mixed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So the nationalists had a mixed composition. Now, number 2. Were you ever at spot number 2, the hospital which is otherwise referred to as Kirurgija? Were you ever there? Did you ever go inside?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that that hospital worked as a surgical ward throughout the war and that the surgical team was led by Dr. Rebac?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know what number 3 is, that it was something called the old hospital and that it worked, it was operational? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw it, but we were never invited to look how it worked, number 2 nor number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did you ask to go inside? Did anybody stop you go inside and looking around?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely, we asked to see the location when it was offered for the first time, but it never happened.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that number 3 was the ear, nose, and mouth, and the psychiatric ward as well, where there were psychiatric patients throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that number 4 was the clinic in Liska street? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: The dispensary.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court why you were able to enter the new hospital whereas somebody would prevent you from looking at numbers 2, 3, and 4? So what would the reason be for you not being allowed to look at those others?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably because the HVO officials, authorities, didn't like us to go there. The other places, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, you are speculating here; is that correct? You said probably because. This is a speculation of yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it has to do with remembrance, Your Honour, because for sure when -- when the proposal was done, we ask, "Okay, let's go there and show us the place what you are talking about," but that never happened. The only thing what we did was we -- we drove there and had a look how it was situated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Sir, can you give me the name of the person in the HVO, the official, the time and place, who told you that you couldn't go into the hospital? When was that? Who told you that and where?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as I said, it was not -- never offered to us. And when it was not offered to us, then it was also not possible for us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. I don't really understand your answer, but never mind. Now, an IC number, please, for this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, for the map with numbers 1 through 6, could we have a number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will become Exhibit IC 633, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now place the small map on the overhead projector for us to have a look at, the one you had previously. We don't need to -- well, we know that number 1 is the Kirurgija. We know that number 2 is the old hospital. All that has been added here is number 4, the health centre. Now, do you know that that was the health centre at number 4 and that it worked throughout the conflict and that it took in patients from the primary health care system? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Under number 5 is the position of the glass bank. Do you see number 5, Witness?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see number 5, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Is that the position of the glass bank?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's hard to see. Maybe it's -- it's better on the aerial picture.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: What about number 6? Is that the gymnasium or secondary school? And you passed by that way frequently. Number 6, the secondary school; right?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And is number 7 Tito's bridge?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Seven.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And we have the directions from which the bullet might have come from the secondary school and glass bank. Now, let's first of all deal with the separation line between the HVO and BH army. Is that the right separation line while you were there, the red line, thick red line passing across the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not complete in my knowledge, but it is, as I very well remember, correct on your aerial photograph. I mean an important part here is not marked on your -- on your sketch.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Would you mark it then?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did the HVO trench go behind the secondary school, that is to say more westerly -- in a more westerly direction?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was this way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: To the best of your recollections, the HVO trench, did it pass behind the secondary school, behind the glass building, or in front of the secondary school building and the glass bank building as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. It's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's not irrelevant as far as we're concerned, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's important to know where the separation line between the warring parties was. First of all, to know where the blue bank building was, and also to know where the Tito Bridge was, to know where the shots were fired from.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think -- I just want to say that we are now officially eating into the time that had been allotted for redirect examination for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. So you need to come to an end, Mr. Praljak. Ask your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that the HVO trench went behind the secondary school building or in front of it, or behind the glass building or in front of it? Which way did the HVO trench stretch, behind or in front? To the west of these two buildings or to the east of these two buildings?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I know, to the east.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Stringer, how much time would you need for redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We're going until 25 minutes after the hour, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think I need 20 minutes of that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So Mrs. Alaburic, are you willing to relinquish the five minutes that remain to Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'll let General Praljak complete his cross-examination, and if there are two minutes left over, then I shall use them if I may.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have an IC number for the map, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This map will become Exhibit IC 634, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have 3D 00703 next, please. 3D 00703. Your Honour, it's a book, a protocol from the hospital. I have it here. You have photocopies of it. It's from the new hospital, and it relates to the period when the gentleman was there. So I'd like him to look at 3D 00703.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The copy of the hospital book has a different 3D number. I'd just like to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1062. And then the table is 00703. Could the witness take a look at the table 3D 7 -- 3D 00703.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, but I don't have it in front of me. The table, yeah? The smaller one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: If you look at the ethnic composition of the patients, you will see that there is Bosniak, Bosniak, Bosniak, and so on. Now, my question is this: When you went to the hospital while you were there, did you ever talk to the patients?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that we were guided once in the hospital and saw the patients.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did you inquire about the national composition of the people coming to the hospital for treatment, that is to say how many patients that the hospital admitted were people that said they were Bosniaks or Croats, that gave their ethnicity as being such? Did you look at the protocol to see whether the nationalists make differences and differentiate between the various ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had knowledge that the specialists were mixed and the patients were mixed as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Were 70 per cent of the specialists Bosniaks as you noted?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- I don't recall percentages.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And I'm referring to P 0229 of your report. And my last question is this: If it is true and correct what it says here in the table that there were Bosniaks and they were coming in from the west bank, because after the 9th of May the -- 1993, the conflict was already underway, how come that there were so many Bosniaks who could come to the hospital if, according to what we have heard, the HVO incarcerated them all or expelled them? Can you explain this fact, that you had such a large number of Bosniaks just in one hospital without primary health care if they had indeed been incarcerated and expelled? Did you deal with that kind of subject? Did you look into it?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I can't answer this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You didn't apply the random sample method in your investigations, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. When you explain me what it means, then probably I can give an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This brings your examination -- cross-examination to an end, General Praljak. Unfortunately, you've run out of time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just want to say how much I regret the fact that I cannot clarify more what a nationalist is by definition, what it means and how much the witness knows about the psychology of warfare, sociology, how certain elements are investigated and studied and so on and so forth. But anyway, thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're beginning to make a speech. Your role is simply to question the witness. Now I will give the floor again to the Prosecution for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Colonel, I want to talk to you just for a few minutes about the hospital, because you were asked about that a lot in a number of the cross-examinations, and I want to ask you to look at one of the -- the exhibits of the Stojic team, 2D 123.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If that could be placed in front of the witness, please. 2D 00123.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is an exhibit that you were shown during your cross-examination; do you recall it?
