utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this is a letter originating from a gentleman who is with the chief of the medical -- main medical staff of HZ HB; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, in this letter, and I think you testified and even written about this yourself in your own reports, indicating that "We have no volunteers, neither among Muslims nor Croat personnel," and that relates to the volunteers possibly going and exchanging positions with those on the east side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And then he's saying: "So far we have better conditions providing care for the wounded population and soldiers." And would you agree with that assessment, that the west-side hospital did in fact have better conditions and facilities?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The west bank hospital had better conditions, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then he suggests: "As we did so many times before that you send your wounded to the HVO war hospitals where they will have completely identical treatment." Now, the date of this letter is the 11th of June in which they're offering to have people come from the west side to the east side; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, let me take you back to the report you made on that same day, which is in the Prosecution binder a the P 2731.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is your report actually of the following day, one day later, on the 12th of June, 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This is the report of the incident in which the Spanish lieutenant, Aguilar was killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, in light of the fact of this incident and in general the security situation in Mostar, what was the likelihood of and the reality of bringing prisoners and other supplies, for example -- well, bringing -- I'm sorry, not prisoners. How feasible and realistic was it to think that you could have actually been able to bring patients and wounded out from the east side to the west side on the 11th of June or even on the 12th of June?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your permission. I consider that the Prosecutor is now asking the witness to speculate. The witness said in his testimony that SpaBat wrote in his report -- wrote his -- its report and asked for agreement, and the witness said that after this date, too, the witness and his team transported medicines to the other side. So what the Prosecutor is asking to do now is to speculate, pure speculation. I want to remind you we had testimony of that before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber is not of that opinion at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So again, witness, the question is: In your view, based on your presence there and involvement, how feasible and realistic was it to think that, in fact, the HVO proposal was something that could be achieved?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as a direct result of the killing of the Spanish lieutenant, UNPROFOR, and especially SpaBat, was very reluctant and actually refusing in the beginning to deal with any transport or escort through the front line. That was a direct result of this happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. So as a result, then, how seriously did you consider these HVO proposals on exchange?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course we actually noted the official point of view, but we doubted at that time that it was feasible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And in fact was --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really have to object. All I want is to indicate that the witness in his report, P 02271, said that he received the letter and the report of 1620. The incident with the Spanish soldier occurred at 1930 hours. So it is quite obvious that this proposal by the HVO was made before the incident took place so everything the witness is now saying on the Prosecutor's asking the witness is quite obviously speculation that, the writer of the document knew that this was impossible even before the incident in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... In light of this observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, very quickly the next -- I'm going to ask the usher to hand you a sleeve, a plastic sleeve. It's got some documents in it. P 2935. And I'm -- I'm sorry, 2941. And this relates to the note about which you testified both on direct and cross-examination. Can you look at the contents of that sleeve and tell us whether this refreshes your recollection about the format of the note as, you know, the original note that you received and the translation that your interpreter made?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I think that, Your Honour, yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Sorry, could we see what the witness is looking at, Your Honour? Perhaps it could be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. As I indicated yesterday, Mr. President, we sent someone to the vault to pull the original note just so that it could be presented before the Trial Chamber and the witness be allowed to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What you see here is the original note and on the back side the translation of our interpreter. The original note is in -- in red colour, and she -- sorry. The translation is in the red colour, and original note, what you see here, is in blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay, for the record I misspoke twice. It is in fact Exhibit P 2935.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So is that, in fact, the note that you received on the 24th of June as indicated?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the original note, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you were --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we see the original note?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I have no objection, Your Honour, if it to be passed around.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked by a number of the -- counsel for a number of the accused about the positions or the official titles that you believed they held during the course of your dealings with them. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And in particular, you were asked about your beliefs as to the specific position that Mr. Pusic held. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And I believe your testimony, as indicated in the reports, was that you had him as a -- the deputy chief of the HVO military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, that belief, tell us where did that come from? What was that based on?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was based on our --

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. Asked and answers several times during the direct and cross-examination. The witness said that he made his conclusions on the basis of the fact that Mr. Pusic was introduced to him at that way. When the question was asked who introduced him, he said he didn't remember the details, but all he -- the witness knows is that's how he was introduced to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Stringer, this is what he said up until now. So what is your additional question adding? Mr. Ibrisimovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I want to say, Mr. President, and I have said this several times, in paragraph -- I've written about it in paragraph 13. I don't know why we're discussing the topic. He said he was -- held a high position in the military police. Whether he was deputy or not is a different matter, and we've dealt with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I could ask another question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You indicated earlier in your testimony that the topics you discussed with Mr. Pusic, at least those related to -- reflected in your reports, related to the Heliodrom and then also the expulsion of Muslim -- or Muslim citizens from East [sic] Mostar. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: All right. Now, based on your understanding of his position, whatever it was, were those issues that he indicated he was in a position to discuss with you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did he ever indicate that those topics were not within his area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but on page 51, line 11, it says that -- it says the expulsion of Muslims from East Mostar. I think that should be corrected. I think my learned friend made a slip there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel. I appreciate your intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So the question again was did he ever indicate to you that he was not in a position or did not have the confidence to discuss those issues with you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And again, did -- were you able to gain access and move around inside the Heliodrom based on the backing or the authorisation that he provided to you?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We needed his approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this isn't redirect. It's examination-in-chief again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Stringer, what are you adding?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me -- let me take the witness. I have one more question about Mr. -- on this subject or this -- this accused, Mr. President. I'll move to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: One of the exhibits that you were shown, Colonel, during the cross-examination, and that is Exhibit P 2496. It's in the Prosecution binder, 2496.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This was an ECMM report not made by your team but one of the other teams; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the Mostar team but the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And I want to take you to the third page of that. And in the top paragraph it says that: "The agreement to allow the ICRC proposed visits has been signed by Pasalic for the armija. Pusic for the HVO said he was not authorised to sign, but an arrangement had been made for Coric, minister for police, to do so." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, despite the spelling do you have an indication or a belief as to who the Coric is that's being referred to there?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the uniform should be an "O".

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's misspelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who is that a reference to?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the speaker.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seem to be having a problem with my microphone. In the original document it says here Curic, Cur, not Cor. And as the witness said that this was drawn up by the team that was in Mostar before he arrived, then I don't think there are any grounds for the witness to say what it should or how it should or should not read because he did not compile the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is does not say Coric but Curic. It's a U.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just going on, Colonel, could I ask you who at that time did you believe was the minister for police that's referred to here?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Coric, I suppose, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could he state that directly, because there's the Ministry of the Interior, including the regular civilian police, and there is the military police, and in the military police there was no post of minister. So it would be a good thing if the Prosecutor would specify what ministry he's referring to and what the name of the ministry -- minister of the interior was at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The military and civilian police and the civilian police was under the MUP. Mr. Milverton when talking about the ministry of police is talking to which one? We don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, have you read this passage now, the reference both to Pusic and then Curic as the minister for police, who in your view is these remarks referring to? And tell us their positions if you recall.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Curic --

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is speculation once again, guesswork.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... The Prosecutor and the witness, please. Ask your question, and we need an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Colonel, I gave you the question. I can give it to you again, if you like. I'm just asking you simply if -- if based on the context here you can tell us who these are references to.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. This is related to a visit, and I got the information from the HVO in Mostar. So it is Mr. Pusic as the deputy and Mr. Curic as chief of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And my last question, the last exhibit I'm going to take you to one of the exhibits of the 2D. It would be in the pink folder there. I ask you to turn to Exhibit 2D 0016.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And this was a letter that was shown to you during your cross-examination, addressed by Mr. Stojic to the Spanish minister of defence. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, turning to the second page, the top paragraph, the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stojic is writing here that based on expert analysis on the type of the weapons and its calibre, it is determined that HVO members could not cause mentioned effects from the distance of their positions and with the weapons they had.

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's talking here about the shooting of Lieutenant Aguilar. He adds: "Finally not even from the most prominent positions at the bank and gymnasium buildings --"

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise, but it is not my intention to upset the proceedings. I understand my colleague's rights, but it is not proper to mention Mr. Stojic at this point. We're talking about an investigation that was conducted and the report of that investigation. Mr. Stojic in this letter presents the report of the investigation which the Spanish Battalion compiled together with the HVO. Now, if you put this into Mr. Stojic's mouth, it takes on quite a different connotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a letter over the signature of Bruno Stojic that was put to the witness by Mr. Stojic's counsel. These are his words. That's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Well, we have the letter. So please ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And the question is this: When Mr. Stojic refers to and makes representations about those positions at the bank and at the gymnasium, are those the same two positions that you discussed with him at the meeting that you testified about earlier?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what is it that he told you about those positions?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said when we asked him about snipers from that positions that he controlled them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did you ever yourself see shots coming from the blue bank building at any time during your stay in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you know yourself that to be an HVO position?

utterances.speaker: ANTOON VAN DER GRINTEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, nothing further.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to intervene at this point and say that we should look at the first page of this document, and on that first page of the document it says that these are the findings of the commission. So I would like that to be taken note of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, fine. If Mr. Stojic is involved, wants to take the floor, he can do so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED STOJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I rarely get up, but these are the findings of the commission on the basis of an investigation undertaken by the Spanish Battalion and the HVO a report was drawn up, and on the basis of that report, Judge Trechsel, I sent a letter to SpaBat and Bruno Stojic was not either at the glass building nor does he know where the positions were. So don't shake your head. You keep shaking your head, but that's how things stand. That's how it was. And I've noticed that for a year now, Your Honours. I have to say that. I've never told a lie in my life, but I compiled this report on the basis of the report by the SpaBat commission and HVO commission. It was a very professional commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: We're not in a phase that we have arguments. We are hearing witnesses and there are different opinions and what you have said we know quite well because we are able to read the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Mr. Stojic, you are -- what you said is now going to be on the record. You explained that this letter is just the conclusions of a commission involving HVO and the Spanish Battalion. This is what you told us, and it's now on the record. I just summarised what you just told us. Now, the hearing is adjourned. Colonel, thank you. I want to express our gratitude on behalf of the Bench to have come testify. I also wish all the best to everyone, and after the vacation we will meet again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 16th day of August, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.31 p.m.
